title: R3 · printable point, ribs to the tip
changes: The last 4 mm of the needle get a width floor of 0.6·d·(1−d/4 mm), where d is the distance to the point: at least 0.9 mm across 1 mm back. Further back the blade is r2's curve. (A first try put the floor on the whole beak and made a wide arrowhead; the reviewer caught it, and it was fixed before this review.)
Grooves run to about 1.5 mm from the point. They stop where the blade is under 1.8 mm across (r2: 2.6 mm); at 1.6 mm, two tip grooves left a pinhole.
A groove is skipped only at corners sharper than 100° (r2: 80°), so the step faces are ribbed through. 99 grooves; still 33 through-holes and one watertight body.
Checked the head-end dots with a close-up render: they were render speckle, not holes.
review: Accepted. The beak follows r2's curve on the photo outline, and the two thin curved needles close cleanly in top.png.
One plain band is left on the jaw face, at the inside corner at the foot of the shoulder below the beak. In robot.png the ribs run through it.
The edge-on taper is even from both sides. side.png hints at a one-sided chisel, but that reading is low-confidence.
The last ~1.5 mm of the jaw edge has no grooves. That is fine: grooving it made pinholes, and the photos can't resolve that area.
The grooves read as a saw-tooth in the dorsal close-up. That is just 0.5 mm grooves at render scale; no change needed.
For the next pass: rib that one inside corner, and check the chisel reading against a clearer side photo. Leave the outline, tip floor, holes and groove depth as they are.
